jobs.description:
Part of your life. Part of tomorrow.

Wir machen das Leben einfacher, sicherer und umweltfreundlicher, mit Technik, die mehr leistet, weniger verbraucht und für alle verfügbar ist. Mikroelektronik von Infineon ist der Schlüssel für eine lebenswerte Zukunft. Wir achten auf schonenden Umgang mit natürlichen Ressourcen und lösen gesellschaftliche Herausforderungen: Effiziente Energienutzung, umweltgerechte Mobilität und Sicherheit in einer vernetzten Welt. 2 Staff Engineer Application Stress Test Methodologies (f/m/div) ID: HRC1166867

Join us at KAI and become a key player in the semiconductor industry, where every design and test brings us closer to a sustainable, electrified future! As our new Staff Engineer specializing in Application Stress Test Methodologies, you¿ll dive into the world of next-generation wide-bandgap power semiconductors, designing innovative test systems that explore performance under extreme conditions.

At KAI, we strive to create pioneering reliability test methods and systems for robust power semiconductor technologies. Your know-how in designing and developing test systems will help us push our technology to its limits while collaborating with a team of innovators.

Your new responsibilities:

Develop and design advanced power electronic circuits through simulations and concept studies

Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to gather and manage system requirements effectively

Transform designs into hardware, overseeing the complete implementation process, and supervising the manufacturing phase

Evaluate and validate designs within an industrial laboratory setting

Lead stress testing using both established and newly developed test systems

Document designs, concepts, and results with clarity and precision

You are a hands-on innovator with a passion for high-performing power electronic systems. You thrive on bringing ideas to life, blending technical understanding with a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Your toolkit for success includes:

Master's / PhD in Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

Strong expertise in SPICE and system-level simulations of power electronic circuits

Proven experience in PCB design using industry-standard tools like ALTIUM Designer

Practical experience with power electronic hardware design, from concept to laboratory validation

Excellent communication skills in English and/or German

The ability to lead and mentor junior team members, fostering a collaborative and innovative workspace

jobs.description: IRC (International Rescue Committee) Germany is seeking aProgram Development & Award Advisor (d/f/m), Latin America- in Berlin, or remote (within Germany) | as soon as possible- in part-time (20 hours/week), increase to full-time in the future might be possible (contingent upon funding) | initially for 2 yearsAbout UsFounded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: "Taking the pulse of our Earth to safeguard a habitable planet."For section 2.1 "Physics of Earthquakes and Volcanoes" (https://www.gfz.de/en/section/physics-of-earthquakes-and-volcanoes/overview) (department “Geophysics (https://www.gfz.de/en/geophysics) ”), we are looking for a:Research scientist (f_m_x) - SeismologyReference Number 11691Earthquakes induced by human activities, such as deep geothermal energy production, can cause ground shaking that raises concerns among local communities. Understanding earthquake source processes and predicting the resulting ground motions, including their uncertainties, are important for assessing seismic impacts and supporting transparent communication with stakeholders.Within the BMWE-funded collaborative project "Seismological Analysis and Societal Relevance of Deep Energy Projects (SAURIER)", GFZ is responsible for the subproject "TRansparent Interpretation and Characterisation of Earthquake RAdiation Patterns through probabilistic moment TensOr inversion and PGV Simulations (TRICERATOPS)". We are looking for a motivated researcher with a strong background in seismology and experience in earthquake source analysis and seismic waveform processing.The successful candidate will contribute to developing and applying probabilistic methods for earthquake source characterisation and physics-based ground motion modelling. The research will focus on quantifying the influence of earthquake source parameters and subsurface structure on predicted ground motions and their uncertainties, with the aim of estimating seismic impact zones.Fraunhofer IEG coordinates SAURIER and brings together seismological and social science research to improve the assessment and communication of induced seismicity.Your responsibilities:- Analyse seismic waveform datasets and determine earthquake source parameters, particularly for small to moderate earthquakes, using probabilistic methods including uncertainty quantification- Integrate earthquake source parameters and their uncertainties into physics-based ground motion simulations using numerical modelling tools such as Pyrocko and its Green's function modelling framework- Investigate the sensitivity of predicted ground motions to source parameters, including focal mechanism, source depth and rupture characteristics, as well as subsurface structure- Develop and validate probabilistic ground motion models for moderate earthquakes and contribute to the estimation of seismic impact zones- Develop, test and document scientific software and reproducible analysis workflows- Develop clear and accessible visualisations of earthquake source characteristics, probabilistic ground motion simulations and estimated seismic impact zones for different target groups, including scientists, authorities and the general public, in collaboration with social science partners at UFZ- Collaborate with project partners and contribute to the interpretation and communication of scientific results- Publish research results in peer-reviewed scientific journals and present findings at national and international conferences- Contribute to project reports, meetings and scientific outreach activitiesAbout You:Essential Qualifications:- A Master's degree (MSc) and a PhD in Earth Science, with a focus on seismology and geophysics- Solid geophysical and seismological background- Experience in local earthquake analysis, including moment tensor inversion- Good programming skills in Python, experience in scientific data processing, and experience in developing, adapting and validating computational methods for seismological research, including the implementation of reproducible workflows in Python- Familiarity with seismology toolboxes (e.g. Pyrocko, ObsPy) and visualisation tools (e.g. GMT, ParaView, QGIS)- Experience in scientific research, demonstrated through a convincing and strong publication record, software contributions and other research outputs appropriate to career stage- Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate scientific results clearly- Experience in collaborative and externally funded research projectsDesirable Qualifications:- Experience in numerical seismic wave propagation or ground motion modelling- Knowledge of probabilistic inversion methods, uncertainty quantification or sensitivity
